lines: In these generated files gitleaks matches only rules that take any string of high entropy, which hashes and minified names are as well, or the curl lines a page of built documentation copies from its source, so the matches are not reported as secrets:
.schemathesis/default/cache/crashes/GET_api_share_token_calendar_events_status_code_conformance_02d14666.json, build output, as .gitignore says: 1 match in 1 commit (generic-api-key).
.schemathesis/default/cache/crashes/GET_api_share_token_feed_external_status_code_conformance_2b7e5334.json, build output, as .gitignore says: 1 match in 1 commit (generic-api-key).
.schemathesis/default/cache/crashes/GET_api_share_token_navigation_response_schema_conformance_480632d7.json, build output, as .gitignore says: 1 match in 1 commit (generic-api-key).
docs/discussion/LICENSING-MODEL.md, build output, as .gitignore says: 1 match in 1 commit (generic-api-key).
docs/features/feed-widget.nl.md, build output, as .gitignore says: 1 match in 1 commit (generic-api-key).
A key a build takes from the environment ends up in such a file too: where one of them has no reason to carry a key, look at it.
In these files gitleaks matches values that stand for a credential, such as admin:admin or <password>, so the matches are not reported as secrets:
The values are the list secrets-placeholders.json of ncmake.
